Activation function.def: A non-linear function applied element-wise between layers (ReLU, GELU, Tanh, Sigmoid). Without it, stacked linear layers collapse into one.

Adam.def: Optimizer that keeps a running mean of each parameter's gradient and of its square, and steps by their ratio, so every parameter gets its own step size.
Adam.hint: Two moving averages plus a bias correction for the first steps.

ArgMax.def: The position of the largest value along the last dimension; turns class scores into a predicted class index.

Asynchronous execution.def: GPU operations return as soon as they are queued and run later in order; reading a value waits for them.

Attention.def: A layer in which each position computes a weighted mix of all positions' values, with weights from query–key similarity.
Attention.hint: Softmax of dot products, then a weighted average.

Autograd.def: The mechanism that records every operation on tensors that require gradients (the tape) and replays it backwards on Backward() to compute all gradients.
Autograd.hint: Reverse-mode application of the chain rule.

Backend.def: The internal engine behind a device (CPU or CUDA) that allocates memory and implements the math primitives.

Backward pass.def: The second half of a training step: gradients flow from the loss back through the recorded operations to the parameters.
Backward pass.hint: Local derivatives multiplied along each path and summed over paths.

Bag of words.def: Representing a text by its words regardless of order, e.g. by averaging their embeddings.

BatchNorm.def: Normalizes each channel with the batch's mean and variance in training and with running averages in evaluation, then scales and shifts.

Bias.def: The learned constant a layer adds to each output, letting it shift its result independently of the input.
Bias.hint: The intercept b in y = wx + b.

Broadcasting.def: Reusing a smaller tensor across the leading dimensions of a larger one, as when a bias vector is added to every row of a batch. In NeuralSharp only + broadcasts.

Buffer.def: Non-trainable tensor state of a module (running statistics, masks), saved and moved with the model but not optimized.

Categorical feature.def: A column whose values are categories (country, product type) rather than quantities; fed to a network through an embedding or one-hot encoding.

Causal mask.def: A mask that hides future positions from attention, so position t sees only positions 0…t; required for next-token prediction.

Cell state.def: The LSTM's second, gated memory vector, carried from step to step alongside the hidden state.

Chain rule.def: The rule for differentiating a composition: the derivative of an outer function applied to an inner one is the outer derivative times the inner derivative. Autograd applies it once per recorded operation.
Chain rule.hint: Rates of change multiply along a chain.
Chain rule.see: Pre-Calc volume Numbers, Shapes, and Functions, function composition; any calculus text for the derivative form

Channel.def: One of the parallel feature maps of an image tensor: 3 for RGB input, the number of filters after a convolution.

CNN.def: Convolutional neural network: a network built mainly from convolution and pooling layers, used for images.

Composite module.def: A module built from other modules, which it lists in Children().

Computation graph.def: The record of which operation produced which tensor, built during the forward pass and consumed by Backward().
Computation graph.hint: A directed graph without cycles; Backward visits it in reverse topological order.

ComputeResources.def: Static class that caps CPU threads and per-device memory and reports memory usage.

Context length.def: The maximum number of positions a sequence model looks at in one pass.

Convolution.def: Sliding a small learned filter over an input and taking the weighted sum at every position.
Convolution.hint: Same weights reused at every position.

Cosine similarity.def: The dot product of two vectors divided by the product of their lengths: 1 for the same direction, 0 for perpendicular, −1 for opposite.
Cosine similarity.hint: The cosine of the angle between the vectors.
Cosine similarity.see: {ch:embedding}; Pre-Calc volume Numbers, Shapes, and Functions, trigonometry

CUDA.def: NVIDIA's platform for general computing on GPUs. NeuralSharp uses only its driver API, which ships with the display driver.

Dense layer.def: A layer in which every output depends on every input through its own weight; Linear in NeuralSharp.

Detach.def: A tensor that shares data with another but has no history, so gradients stop there.

Device.def: Where a tensor's numbers live and where operations on it run: Device.Cpu or Device.Cuda(n). Operands of one operation must share a device.

Dispose.def: Returning a tensor's memory to the device cache immediately (using calls it automatically).

Dropout.def: Randomly zeroing a fraction of values during training to reduce overfitting; disabled in evaluation mode.

Embedding.def: A learned vector for each id of a vocabulary, looked up from a table.

Epoch.def: One full pass over the training data. Training usually runs many epochs.

Evaluation mode.def: Module state for inference, set by Eval(): dropout is off and normalization uses its running statistics. Train() switches back.

Factory method.def: A method that builds a model the same way every time, shared by the training and inference programs so saved weights always fit.

Feature map.def: The output channel of one convolution filter: where in the image that filter's pattern appears.

Feed-forward network.def: The two-layer MLP (D → 4D → D with GELU) applied to every position inside a transformer block.

Filter.def: A small learned weight array (k×k over all input channels) that a convolution slides over the input; also called a kernel.

Finalizer.def: A .NET safety net that frees a tensor's memory if it was never disposed; it runs late and unpredictably.

Finite difference.def: An estimate of a derivative from function values: (f(x + h) − f(x − h)) / 2h. Used to check gradients.
Finite difference.hint: The slope of a short chord approximates the slope of the tangent.
Finite difference.see: {ch:autograd}; Pre-Calc volume Numbers, Shapes, and Functions, rates of change

Flatten.def: Merging all dimensions after the batch into one: [N, C, H, W] → [N, C·H·W].

Float32.def: The 32-bit floating-point number type (float) in which every tensor stores and computes its values; about 7 significant digits.

Gate.def: A sigmoid-valued vector (between 0 and 1) that scales how much of a signal passes; the mechanism of LSTM and GRU memory.

GELU.def: Gaussian error linear unit: a smooth ReLU-like activation, standard in transformers.

GFLOP/s.def: Billions of floating-point operations per second; the usual measure of arithmetic throughput.

Global average pooling.def: Averaging each channel over all positions: [N, C, H, W] → [N, C].

Gradient.def: For every parameter, how much the loss changes when that parameter is nudged; the optimizer moves each parameter against its gradient.
Gradient.hint: The vector of partial derivatives; its negative points downhill.
Gradient.see: {ch:autograd}; Activation Functions volume for gradient effects of each activation

Gradient accumulation.def: Summing gradients over several smaller batches before one optimizer step, to emulate a larger batch.

GRU.def: Gated recurrent unit: a recurrent layer with reset and update gates and a single state; lighter than an LSTM.

Hidden state.def: The vector a recurrent layer carries from one time step to the next and outputs.

im2col.def: Unfolding every convolution window into a row of a matrix so the whole convolution becomes one matrix product.

Initialization.def: How weights are set before training. NeuralSharp uses Xavier-uniform for Linear, He-uniform for Conv2d, N(0, 1) for embeddings, and zeros for biases.
Initialization.hint: Keep the size of signals roughly equal from layer to layer.

InUse.def: Bytes of device memory currently held by live tensors, as reported by MemoryUsage.InUse.

Inverted dropout.def: Dropout that scales surviving values by 1/(1 − p) during training, so nothing needs rescaling at inference.

Kernel.def: A function that runs on the GPU in many parallel threads, one launch per operation.

KV cache.def: Stored keys and values of already-processed positions, so generating each new token only computes the new position.

Lambda.def: A layer that wraps any tensor function, e.g. averaging over time.

LayerNorm.def: Normalizes each sample over its last dimension, then scales and shifts per feature; independent of the batch.

Leaf.def: A tensor created directly rather than by a recorded operation: data, targets, parameters. Gradients are kept on leaves.

Linear.def: NeuralSharp's dense layer: y = x · W + b over the last dimension.

Logits.def: Raw, unnormalized class scores from the last Linear layer; softmax or sigmoid turns them into probabilities.

Loss.def: A single number that measures how wrong the predictions are; training minimizes it.

LSTM.def: Long short-term memory: a recurrent layer with input, forget and output gates and a separate cell state.

Matrix product.def: The product of an [m, k] and a [k, n] matrix: each output element is the dot product of a row and a column. MatMul in NeuralSharp.

Max pooling.def: Keeping the largest value of each window of a feature map; shrinks the map and adds tolerance to small shifts.

Memory cache.def: Freed device memory blocks kept per size for reuse, so repeated steps allocate nothing new.

Memory leak.def: Memory that is never freed because tensors created repeatedly are neither disposed nor scoped; seen as InUse growing every step.

Memory limit.def: A cap on tensor memory per device set through ComputeResources; crossing it throws ResourceLimitExceededException.

MLP.def: Multilayer perceptron: a stack of dense layers with activations between them.

Module.def: Anything that maps input tensors to output tensors and may own parameters: a layer, an activation, or a Sequential of them.

Momentum (BatchNorm).def: The weight of the newest batch in BatchNorm's running averages (0.1 by default).

MSE.def: Mean squared error: the average of the squared differences between prediction and target. The default loss for regression.
MSE.hint: Squaring punishes large errors more than small ones.

Multi-head attention.def: Several attention computations in parallel on slices of the vectors, recombined by a linear layer.

NCHW.def: The image tensor layout used by NeuralSharp: batch, channels, height, width.

NoGrad.def: A scope in which operations are not recorded for autograd; used for inference and evaluation.

Normal distribution.def: The bell-shaped distribution of values around a mean with a given standard deviation; used to initialize weights and add noise.
Normal distribution.hint: About 68% of values lie within one standard deviation of the mean.

One-hot.def: A vector of zeros with a single 1 at the position of a class index.

Optimizer.def: The object that updates parameters from their gradients: Sgd, Adam, AdamW.

Overfitting.def: Learning the training data too specifically, so the training loss keeps falling while the validation loss rises.

Padding.def: (1) Zeros added around an image so a convolution can cover its borders. (2) Filler ids (usually 0) that bring token sequences to a common length.

Parameter.def: A tensor the network learns (weights and biases). Created with gradient tracking on and exposed through Module.Parameters().

Pooling.def: Combining many values into one: max or average over an image window, or mean over a sequence.

Positional encoding.def: Fixed sine and cosine patterns added to token vectors so attention can tell positions apart.
Positional encoding.hint: Each dimension oscillates at a different frequency along the positions.

Pre-norm.def: Placing LayerNorm before each transformer sub-block (inside the residual branch), which makes deep stacks train stably.

PTX.def: NVIDIA's portable GPU assembly language. NeuralSharp writes its kernels in PTX; the driver compiles them for the installed GPU.

Query, key, value.def: The three projections of each position in attention: the query is compared with every key; the matching values are mixed.

Rank.def: The number of dimensions of a tensor: 0 for a scalar, 1 for a vector, 2 for a matrix.

Recurrent layer.def: A layer that processes a sequence step by step, carrying a hidden state (LSTM, GRU).

Reference counting.def: Tracking how many tensors share a memory block, so it is freed only when the last one is.

Regularization.def: Anything that discourages overfitting: dropout, weight decay, more data, early stopping.

ReLU.def: Activation that keeps positive inputs and replaces negative ones with zero. Cheap and the usual default in deep networks; a unit whose input stays negative stops learning.
ReLU.hint: Gradient is 1 for positive inputs and 0 otherwise.

Reserved.def: InUse + Cached: all memory the library currently holds from the system on a device.

Reshape.def: Viewing the same data with a different shape (same element count, same order); no copy.

Residual connection.def: Adding a block's input to its output (x + f(x)), so information and gradients can bypass the block.

Return sequences.def: The recurrent-layer option to output the state at every step ([N, T, H]) instead of only the last ([N, H]).

Row-major.def: Storage order in which the last dimension changes fastest: a matrix is stored row after row.

Running statistics.def: Moving averages of each channel's mean and variance that BatchNorm keeps for evaluation mode.

Saturation.def: When an activation such as sigmoid or tanh flattens out for large inputs, so its slope, and the gradient through it, is nearly zero.

Scalar.def: A single number; as a tensor, rank 0 with shape [].

Scaled dot-product attention.def: softmax(Q·Kᵀ / √d) · V: scores from query–key dot products, scaled by the square root of the head width.
Scaled dot-product attention.hint: Scaling keeps the softmax from saturating as d grows.

Sequence.def: An ordered list of items (tokens, measurements) processed by recurrent or attention layers; shape [N, T, F] or [N, T].

Sequential.def: The container module that runs its layers in order.

SGD.def: Stochastic gradient descent: move each parameter by −learning rate × gradient, optionally with momentum.
SGD.hint: Step downhill in proportion to the slope.

Shape.def: The list of a tensor's dimension lengths, outermost first, e.g. [32, 1, 28, 28].

Sigmoid.def: Activation that squashes any number into the range 0 to 1; used for probabilities of yes/no outputs.
Sigmoid.hint: S-shaped curve; its slope is largest at 0 and vanishes far from it.
Sigmoid.see: Activation Functions volume, Sigmoid; Pre-Calc volume, exponential functions

SIMD.def: Single instruction, multiple data: CPU instructions that process 4 to 16 floats at once. The CPU backend uses them through Vector<float>.

Softmax.def: Turns a row of scores into probabilities: exponentiate each score and divide by the row total.
Softmax.hint: Larger scores get exponentially larger shares; the row sums to 1.
Softmax.see: {ch:tensors}; Activation Functions volume, Softmax; Pre-Calc volume, exponential functions

Standardization.def: Shifting and scaling values to mean 0 and standard deviation 1.

Streaming multiprocessor.def: One of the GPU's independent processing units (SMs); a GPU has from a few to over a hundred, each running many threads.

Stride.def: The step between successive positions of a convolution or pooling window; stride 2 halves the output size.

Synchronize.def: Waiting until all queued work on a device has finished: device.Synchronize().

Tanh.def: Activation that squashes any number into the range −1 to 1; zero-centred, a good default for small networks.

Tensor.def: An n-dimensional array of 32-bit floats with a shape and a device. The basic data type of the library.

TensorScope.def: A using block that disposes every tensor created inside it when it ends, returning device memory to the pool.

Token.def: One unit of text given an id: a word, a sub-word or a character.

Training mode.def: Module state during training (Train()): dropout active, BatchNorm using batch statistics.

Transformer.def: An architecture of stacked blocks, each attention plus a feed-forward network with residual connections and normalization.

Unknown token.def: A reserved id for words not in the vocabulary.

Vanishing gradient.def: Gradients shrinking as they pass back through many layers or time steps, so early parts learn slowly; gates, residual connections and normalization counter it.

View.def: A tensor that shares another tensor's memory (from Reshape, Flatten, Detach).

Vocabulary.def: The set of ids a model knows (words, characters, categories) and the mapping to them.

Weight.def: A learned multiplier; a layer's weights form a matrix or filter bank.

Weights file.def: The binary file written by Save: every parameter and buffer with its shape, but not the architecture.

XOR.def: Exclusive or: the output is 1 when exactly one of two inputs is 1. The smallest problem a network without a hidden layer cannot solve.
XOR.hint: The two classes cannot be split by one straight line.
XOR.see: Activation Functions volume, XOR impossibility chapter
